content.comment_body: Hello everyone, could you provide an example of how to connect two [product_name] modules with article number [article_no]? I would like to expand my output to reach 32. Thanks and regards to all.

Hi, here are some options: 1. Connect using digital inputs/outputs. 2. Use a [product_name] ASi module, which requires a master and allows up to 4 digital inputs and 4 digital outputs to be exchanged. 3. Use the [product_name] KNX/EIB option, making use of any unused digital I/Os on your [product_name] module. Check [url] for manuals and more details.

Adding to [user_name]'s response, here is a general overview for connecting two or more [product_name] modules as discussed in the forum: Coupling or data exchange via EIB bus is a possible but costly solution and has been frequently debated in the forum—try searching for terms like 'EIB [product_name]'. Alternatives for coupling and data exchange usually rely on suitable I/O connections. For high switching frequency digital exchanges, transistor outputs are recommended. You can also wire digital or analog inputs in parallel across multiple [product_name] modules. The next step would be transmitting signals or commands via digital or analog lines from one to others. Bidirectional linking is possible by connecting inputs and outputs of different modules with varied wiring configurations such as individual, serial, or star-shaped layouts, depending on the application. Ideally, distribute program functions among modules so that only minimal data communication is needed, such as for alarms or triggers. Modules should handle analog signal processing independently, and only pass on needed digital signals to other modules. For multiple digital signals, consider using binary codes to minimize wiring—codes with n lines allow for 2^n values. A digital signal from one module can also receive multiple data sets at the same input via coding. If you need to transfer more complex data or further reduce the number of lines, simple communication protocols such as impulse-count commands or short serial data packets (with or without dedicated clock lines) can be used, though this requires suitable circuitry within all connected [product_name] modules.
